name: Named continents
description: Pads that forgot they were pads. Cities that hung. Hearths first.

pages.title: Named continents
pages.text:
The old maps did not say *island*.\
They named continents the way you name a house: by who kept the hearth, by which river had manners, by which city hung over which Strand-knot.\
A pad that had forgotten it was a pad got a name.

pages.title: Continue
pages.text: A name was a promise that the inspection had gone well for long enough to stop calling it a pad.

pages.title: Cities that hung
pages.text: Markets sat on lattice, not bedrock. Stairs went down to the under-thread and up to the weather-road. You could walk a street and never think about the drop because the Soil Strand ran under the cobbles the way warmth runs under a well-kept floor.

pages.title: Continue
pages.text: Hanging felt like standing. That was the trick, and it was work.

pages.title: Hearths as first ...
pages.text: Before Stone named shards, before Clock sang a factory, a Pad-keeper banked heat in thin dirt and called it a world. The hearth is the first physics. A continent is a hearth that got out of hand in the useful direction.

pages.title: Continue
pages.text: Seat Soil and you are not founding a nation. You are reminding a scrap of dirt that it used to be allowed to stay warm.
